criteria.reason: Persistent sudden painless monocular vision loss beginning two hours ago requires immediate emergency eye and possible stroke assessment. The draft directs ED attendance now without waiting; no unresolved prerequisite delays that assessment.

Immediate emergency assessment is proportionate to possible retinal arterial occlusion or retinal detachment; messaging or routine assessment cannot meet the time-sensitive examination requirement. Ambulance transport is offered rather than universally required, and self-driving is discouraged.

Onset, laterality, persistence, pain denial and age are grounded in the original message. Alternative diagnoses remain possibilities; additional neurologic symptoms, headache and measurements are explicitly unknown rather than invented.

Supplied passages support the CRAO presentation and stroke-equivalent urgency, retinal detachment differential, and immediate hospital assessment for possible ischemic symptoms. The draft acknowledges source limitations and does not present the specific diagnosis as confirmed.

New weakness or speech difficulty triggers immediate 911 activation, while the existing vision loss already triggers ED attendance now. The instructions are feasible and do not make current care conditional on deterioration.
No issued question or required clarification delays emergency attendance; the patient is explicitly told not to wait.
The draft directs care to the emergency department without claiming an accepted handoff, booking, coordination, or response guarantee.

transportReview.draftQuote: Go to an emergency department now — do not wait.
